intro: A drawer at Bletchley Park was found to have a false bottom. Beneath it: a stack of intercepts that were never logged, each one pinned to a different page of a crossword. The codebreakers who filed them were men of habits, and among their habits the strangest was how they signed their work—never a full name, never a seal, but a single stroke on the corner, the same stroke they used on the margins of their own notebooks, the same stroke they would sometimes press into the blotting paper left on the desk. One of them, they say, could read the whole room by that mark alone, and would nod to himself when the day’s last sheet bore the right one. The papers have sat there ever since, waiting for the hand that knows them.
echo: One wonder of the ancient world stood astride the harbour at Rhodes; its namesake stood in Block H.

puzzles.title: The Crib
puzzles.flavor: Fenced in, and copied out in a hurry.

blocks.text: NEENT AEIOD EOYXT DOEET FRHPE STNRF UNBDP CAYTG HSSTR ZJSEO RQCOE NOIOI UWEY

hints: All the right letters are here, just out of order. Could they have been written along a path that goes up and down?

puzzles.title: Herivel Tip
puzzles.flavor: Three letters to a strip, and a note of how long each word was.
hints: The strips are alphabetised, not in order. The word lengths say where the breaks fall. Which strip could start the sentence?

puzzles.title: Menu
puzzles.flavor: The operator never once took a breath. Whatever you find, it was said on the way out, not the way in.

meta.title: Meta: Hut Eight
meta.flavor: The last lock takes every signature at once.
